distinguishing_features: Compliant elastomer (polyurethane) lining applied at the elbow wear site to absorb particle impact energy
Curved transition lip extending into the straight section to re-attach separated flow and reduce impingement angle
Viscoelastic energy dissipation lowering transmitted peak contact stress below substrate fatigue/erosion threshold
Geometric coupling of the compliant layer to secondary-flow separation rather than material hardening
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce wall penetration and erosion-fatigue spall in a pneumatic conveying elbow caused by particle impingement, without relying on harder or thicker sacrificial material.
parsed.viable_reason: Elastomer linings and flow-conditioning lips are physically sound and commonly deployed in abrasive-slurry and pneumatic handling, so the mechanism is feasible and testable at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The prior art is entirely monitoring/control/chemistry-based and does not teach compliant-lining-plus-flow-reattachment geometry, so the distinguishing mechanism is not an obvious application of the closest art.
